config.title: Nested Routes & Protected Routes

intro.title: Nested Routes & Protected Routes
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular application with a dashboard that has nested pages and a login-protected admin section. You'll learn how to use Angular's Router to define nested routes for organizing complex layouts and implement a route guard to protect sensitive routes from unauthorized access. The main technologies involved are the Angular Router, route configuration, and a custom CanActivate guard. By the end, you'll understand how to structure multi-level navigation and secure parts of your application based on user authentication.
intro.usecase: Nested and protected routes are essential for building complex, secure applications like admin dashboards or customer portals. For example, in a dashboard, you might have a main layout with a sidebar, and nested routes for sub-pages like 'Analytics', 'User Management', or 'Settings' that load within the same view. Protected routes ensure that only authenticated users can access sensitive areas, such as payment pages or account settings, redirecting unauthorized visitors to a login screen. This pattern keeps the UI organized and secure, mimicking real-world apps like banking platforms or project management tools where navigation is hierarchical and access is controlled.

objectives: Configure nested route structures in Angular Router to organize hierarchical views
Implement route guards to control access to protected application sections
Construct modular child components that render within parent route outlets
Apply routerLink directives to navigate between nested route levels
Initialize route parameters to pass data between parent and child routes
Integrate authentication checks with route guards for conditional navigation
Manipulate router configuration to establish both public and protected route hierarchies

steps.title: Define parent route component (Dashboard)
steps.instruction: Create a standalone DashboardComponent with a basic template that will serve as the parent component for nested routes. Use the @Component decorator with selector 'app-dashboard' and a template containing a heading.
steps.hint: Remember to import Component from '@angular/core' (already done) and use @Component decorator with selector and template properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: A DashboardComponent class is created with proper Angular component structure and a basic template.
successCriteria: DashboardComponent is defined as a standalone component with selector 'app-dashboard' and contains a template with at least a heading element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the DashboardComponent but it might be missing the selector, template, or proper export. Check that you have all required parts.
steps.feedbackWrong: The DashboardComponent wasn't created correctly. Make sure to use the @Component decorator with selector 'app-dashboard' and include a basic template.

steps.title: Define child route components (Overview and Settings)
steps.instruction: Create a standalone Angular component named OverviewComponent with a template that displays a heading 'Overview Page'.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator to define a component. The template can be a simple string with an <h2> element.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a new OverviewComponent class that can be used as a child route component.
successCriteria: OverviewComponent is defined with @Component decorator and displays 'Overview Page' in its template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've defined the component with @Component decorator and included the template with the heading.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you used the @Component decorator and included the template.

steps.title: Configure main application routes
steps.instruction: Define a constant named 'appRoutes' that is an array of route objects. Add one route object with path 'dashboard' and component set to DashboardComponent.
steps.hint: Use the Routes type from '@angular/router' to type the array. The route object should have properties 'path' and 'component'.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a properly typed routes array with a route configuration for the dashboard path.
successCriteria: The appRoutes constant is defined as an array with one route object that has path 'dashboard' and component DashboardComponent.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure appRoutes is an array with one route object containing both 'path' and 'component' properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The route configuration is incomplete. Check that you've defined appRoutes as an array with the correct route object structure.

steps.title: Configure nested routes for Dashboard
steps.instruction: In the appRoutes array, add a children property to the Dashboard route that contains route objects for the Overview and Settings components.
steps.hint: The children property should be an array of route objects, each with a path and component property.

steps.title: Create navigation links in Dashboard
steps.instruction: In the DashboardComponent template, add two navigation links using routerLink directives: one for the 'overview' child route and one for the 'settings' child route.
steps.hint: Use the routerLink directive with the relative path to each child route. For example, routerLink='overview'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The DashboardComponent template will include two navigation links that allow navigation between the nested child routes.
successCriteria: DashboardComponent template contains two <a> elements with routerLink directives pointing to 'overview' and 'settings'.

steps.expectedOutcome: An AuthGuard service is created with CanActivate interface implementation and a canActivate method returning true.
successCriteria: AuthGuard service exists with @Injectable decorator, implements CanActivate interface, and has canActivate method returning boolean true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your service implements CanActivate interface and has a canActivate method that returns a boolean.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AuthGuard service isn't implemented correctly. Check that you have the @Injectable decorator, implement CanActivate, and include the canActivate method.

steps.title: Add canActivate to protected route
steps.instruction: In the Settings route configuration inside the children array, add a canActivate property with the AuthGuard service to protect this route.
steps.hint: Add canActivate: [AuthGuard] to the Settings route object. This will apply route protection using the guard service you created earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Settings route will now be protected by the AuthGuard service, requiring authentication before navigation.
successCriteria: The Settings route configuration includes canActivate: [AuthGuard] property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added canActivate: [AuthGuard] to the Settings route object inside the children array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Settings route should have canActivate: [AuthGuard] added to its configuration to apply route protection.

steps.title: Create login component
steps.instruction: Create a LoginComponent with a basic login form template that includes an email input field, a password input field, and a submit button.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator to define the component with selector 'app-login' and a template containing the form elements.
steps.expectedOutcome: A LoginComponent class is created with a basic login form template.
successCriteria: LoginComponent is defined with selector 'app-login' and a template containing email input, password input, and a submit button.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but make sure it has the correct selector and includes all required form elements in the template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The LoginComponent is not properly defined. Ensure you use the @Component decorator with selector 'app-login' and a template with the login form.

steps.title: Add redirect for unauthorized access
steps.instruction: Update the AuthGuard service to redirect users to the login route when authentication fails instead of just returning false.
steps.hint: Inject the Router service in the AuthGuard constructor and use router.navigate(['/login']) in the canActivate method before returning false.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthGuard service will now redirect unauthorized users to the login page when they try to access protected routes.
successCriteria: AuthGuard's canActivate method includes router.navigate(['/login']) call before returning false
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to include both the router injection and the navigate call in the canActivate method before returning false.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AuthGuard needs to redirect users. Inject Router in the constructor and use router.navigate(['/login']) in the canActivate method when authentication fails.
